turkey_specific_content:
Almost the whole page is Turkey- and sales-specific, so the EN page should be a rewrite, not a translation:
- Positioning: 'Türkiye'ye yönelik Türkçe astroloji sitesi' (lines 129, 160); 'Dil ve kapsam: Tamamen Türkçe; Türkiye'deki 81 il…' (line 144).
- Prices in TL everywhere: lines 129, 142, 158, 160, plus JSON-LD Offers priceCurrency 'TRY' (line 16).
- Legal: KVKK Aydınlatma Metni and Mesafeli Satış Sözleşmesi (FAQ, line 160); the cookie banner links to the Turkish /gizlilik-kvkk.html (line 168).
- Organization JSON-LD (line 16): areaServed 'TR', knowsLanguage 'tr', a Shopier store in sameAs, inLanguage 'tr-TR'.
- Turkish date format 'Güncelleme: 28 Eylül 2026' (line 127) and informal 'sen' address throughout.

How to adapt for a global audience:
1. Position /en/ as 'free astrology calculators in English'.
2. Keep the universal, credible method paragraph (line 147): tropical zodiac, Placidus houses, high-precision ephemeris cross-checked with Swiss Ephemeris, Lahiri ayanamsa for Vedic. Mention only methods that EN tools actually use.
3. Keep the principles (not fate, your data is yours) and the contact email.
4. Say plainly that Instagram content is in Turkish.
5. Add one neutral line such as 'Our in-depth personalised reports are currently available in Turkish only.' Do not link to them.
6. Rewrite the JSON-LD: AboutPage with inLanguage 'en' and an Organization without hasOfferCatalog. knowsLanguage ['tr','en'], drop areaServed TR, drop Shopier.
7. Drop the FAQ, or rewrite it as 3 short EN questions (What is this site? How are charts calculated? How do I contact you?) and update the FAQPage JSON-LD to match.
8. EU visitors: menu.js loads GA4 for everyone in 'bilgilendirme modu' (inform-only, no consent). An English/EU audience raises GDPR consent questions, and EN needs at least an English privacy notice instead of the KVKK link.
9. Pre-existing inconsistency to fix in the TR source too: line 133 says '30 ücretsiz araç', lines 129 and 160 and the meta say 32.
The page never mentions the third-party site the user asked to keep off the site. The rewrite must not add it either.

rationale:
This is the site's About/brand page (AboutPage + Organization + FAQPage JSON-LD). It is not a tool.

Why it is weak as a phase-1 SEO page:
- Search demand: English searches for it are essentially navigational brand queries for 'Astro Yuvam', which has no English brand awareness. It will bring almost no organic traffic, so English search potential is low and so is competition (only the brand query).
- Content: about 809 visible words, but roughly 70% is selling the 18 Turkish-only PDF reports with TL prices, KVKK/distance-sales references, Asterna and Turkey positioning. All of that must be dropped under the 'EN must not sell Turkish reports' rule.

Why it is still cheap and low-risk:
- Translation risk is minimal: no tool logic, no fetch(), and only one Turkish string in inline JS ('Hesabım' in the session-check script, line 122).
- The surrounding shell (menu.js, asterna-widget.js, pwa.js, cookie banner) is shared work every EN page needs anyway. Asterna must be excluded on EN because /api/asterna returns free-form Turkish AI prose that also pitches the Turkish reports.
- The real job is a rewrite of roughly 300-400 words: method (tropical/Placidus, ephemeris cross-checked with Swiss Ephemeris), principles, contact, a 'reports currently Turkish only' note, and cleaned JSON-LD.

Recommendation: do not spend one of the 6-9 phase-1 slots on it. Those slots should go to client-side tools with real English demand. Do ship a short, rewritten /en/about.html alongside phase 1 as a supporting page linked from the EN footer and language switcher. An English section with no English About/contact or privacy information looks thin and weak on trust (E-E-A-T). This page and an English privacy/cookie notice are infrastructure, not traffic pages.
